title: System-wide hang/freeze on dual GPU laptop when idle or switching windows (Godot 4.x)
body:
### Tested versions

Godot version:
- v4.3.stable (also reproducible in v4.2 and v4.1)
Things I have already tried:
- Clearing DirectX and Godot shader caches.
- Forcing "High Performance" GPU in Windows Graphics settings.
- Using --rendering-driver opengl3 (Compatibility mode).
- Enabling "Single Window Mode" in Editor Settings.
- Observation: The freeze still occurs even in Compatibility mode if left idle long enough.

### System information

- System information: - CPU: Intel Core i5-8250U - GPU 1: Intel(R) UHD Graphics 620 (Integrated) - GPU 2: NVIDIA GeForce MX130 (Dedicated) - OS: Windows 10/11 - Driver: Latest Windows Update / NVIDIA Game Ready Drivers

### Issue description


Issue description:
- The Godot editor causes a total system hang (hard freeze) requiring a manual power-button shutdown. This issue is specific to Godot 4.x. While the editor may work for a few minutes, the freeze consistently occurs under the following conditions:

- Idling: Leaving the editor open and untouched for 1-2 minutes.
- Window Switching: Moving focus away from Godot to another application.
- Tooltips: Sometimes triggered by hovering over UI elements that spawn tooltips.

Note: When the freeze occurs, the laptop fans continue to spin at a high rate even if a software shutdown is attempted, suggesting a kernel-level GPU driver deadlock. This setup previously ran Godot 4.3 without issues, suggesting a regression caused by recent driver/OS updates interacting with Godot’s Vulkan implementation.



### Steps to reproduce


Steps to reproduce:
- Open any Godot 4.x project using the Forward+ or Mobile renderer.
- Interact with the editor for 30 seconds.
- Alt-Tab to another window (like a web browser) or leave the computer idle.
- The system will become completely unresponsive.




### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

 Minimal reproduction project:
 - N/A - Occurs even with a completely empty project.
